and survey points, wallboards that turn their own pages, tickets that stay with the colleague they were given to, server readiness and recovery drills, and a large round of reliability and security work.

Incentives: a challenge can now be won by everyone who reaches its target, or by the top agents for the period (you choose how many; agents level at the last place all win). One incentive can cover several teams and carries its prize, such as a day off or a cash bonus. Each running incentive shows its leaderboard on Gamification and on the agent's My points, and its winners when it ends; the result is marked provisional until the last day's late work is counted.

Points for good customer experience: a new measure, Survey answers at or above a score, gives points for each survey answer at or above the score you choose, for one kind of survey or for all of them, so low scores never earn the same as high ones.

Wallboards: each board has its own Turn pages setting, how many seconds a page stays up when the tiles need more than one page. A screen showing a wallboard's TV link now loads platform updates by itself, so it never needs reloading by hand.

Tickets stay with the colleague they were given to: transferring an email moves its ticket to the colleague as well, also for emails that came in through an automatic message flow. Resolving or closing a ticket while a colleague is working on its email now says who has it and goes ahead only if you confirm; the same applies to macros, changing many tickets at once and a major incident's linked tickets.

Screens that keep up with tickets and the office phone system: ticket lists, the Floor and the office panel now change the moment a ticket is assigned, transferred or escalated, or a colleague's office phone changes state.

Legacy diallers: the import and the compatible API for moving from an older dialler are now called Import from a legacy dialler and the Legacy dialler API. Existing connections keep working at their current addresses.

For platform operators

Server readiness: Platform, Servers checks every server against what its role needs (versions, services, disk, memory, clock, the limits calls and many connections need, certificates, backups, replication and cluster health) and shows Ready, Needs attention or Not ready with the exact fix. A server that is not ready cannot finish joining, and an update waits rather than install onto a server with a disk, clock, backup or certificate problem. The limits calls need are now set by install, join and every update.

Recovery drills and restore tests: a drill fails one part of the platform at a time and measures how long it takes to serve again and whether anything was lost; results show on Platform, Servers against their targets. Every Sunday a restore test restores the newest backup, from the off-site copy when there is one, into a scratch copy and records how old the backup was and how long recovery took. Production drills are run by an operator in a quiet window.

Updates that do not disturb calls: the SIP edge is no longer restarted by every update; a change to it waits for a moment with no calls. Two updates can no longer run at once, a failed automatic update is not retried, the nightly switch restart never takes out the only working switch, and a rollback restores the server's scripts as well. Every release now comes with a list of its components and is stopped if a part has a critical security weakness that already has a fix.

Fixes: signing in with Microsoft no longer accepts an invitation by email address alone; a WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram account can only be connected by the organisation that owns it; addresses entered for outside services cannot point inside the platform; a call server that stops answering is taken out of rotation at once; a customer's answer is never lost to a brief database interruption; transfers and connects under way are finished before a worker restarts; and errors on the agent de"}
